1.explanation: The only place in the repo that defines the TeX/LaTeX language grammar is src/languages/latex.js. In that file the opening \{ and closing \} are declared as simple begin/end delimiters whose contents aren’t re-scanned against the standard LaTeX sub-modes. That is precisely why nothing inside braces gets highlighted. To fix this bug, latex.js must be updated so that its brace mode includes the normal set of LaTeX sub-rules rather than treating the whole block as an opaque literal.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting LaTeX source with highlight.js, any commands or markup inside a pair of {…} aren’t parsed with the normal LaTeX rules. Instead, the entire braced chunk is treated as a single literal, so inner tokens like \TeX, \, \! or \~ go unrecognized and un-highlighted. In the user’s screenshots you can see \eTiX, \TeX, \frac, \! and \~ lose their syntax coloring whenever they appear inside braces.

2.explanation: The only place in the repository that governs how LaTeX is tokenized is src/languages/latex.js. In that file, braces are currently defined as a simple begin/end pair without any nested “contains” rules, so their interior is never recursed into for further highlighting. To fix this bug, latex.js must be updated so that the brace modes include the full set of LaTeX sub-modes (commands, math, text, etc.) rather than treating the entire {...} region as a flat string.
2.bug_scenario: In Highlight.js’s LaTeX mode, any code inside braces {…} is currently treated as one undifferentiated block (like a string literal) and its contents are not parsed or highlighted using the normal LaTeX rules. As shown in the provided screen-shots, macros such as \eTiX and \TeX in the first line, and commands like \! or \~ inside text or math contexts, are left unstyled when enclosed within { }. In a second example, constructs inside math-mode braces (after \frac or inside \mathcal{…}) likewise never receive proper command or keyword highlighting. The desired behavior is for everything inside braces—whether text, math, or macro definitions—to be lexed and highlighted just as code outside them.
